title: How fast the world would warm
who: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), First Assessment Report
forecast: About 0.3 °C per decade if emissions carried on as usual, with a range of 0.2 to 0.5
note: Below the central estimate but inside the stated range. The forecast was for a world where emissions carried on as usual. EarthOS worked out the observed rate as the straight-line trend of NASA's yearly averages from 1990 to 2025.
forecast_source: IPCC First Assessment Report, Working Group I summary (1990)
outcome_source: NASA GISTEMP v4 global land-ocean index

title: World population in 2000
note: 3.6% too high, 42 years ahead. The UN's 2024 revision puts the 2000 figure at about 6.2 billion, which makes the 1958 forecast closer still.
forecast_source: US National Academies, Beyond Six Billion (2000), chapter 2
outcome_source: US National Academies, Beyond Six Billion (2000), chapter 2

title: Countries with nuclear weapons
who: President John F. Kennedy, press conference
note: A warning, not a model: Kennedy said it while pressing for a nuclear test-ban treaty, which was agreed later that year. Warnings that lead to action can look wrong afterwards.
forecast_source: Arms Control Association, Daryl G. Kimball (2013)
outcome_source: Federation of American Scientists, Status of World Nuclear Forces (2026)

title: Prices of five metals, a test of scarcity
who: Paul Ehrlich, in a wager with Julian Simon
forecast: Chromium, copper, nickel, tin and tungsten would cost more in 1990, after inflation
note: One decade proves little: over other ten-year periods since 1900, each side would have won about half the time.
forecast_source: Our World in Data, Hannah Ritchie (2025)
outcome_source: Our World in Data, Hannah Ritchie (2025)

title: An AI scoring gold at the Maths Olympiad by 2025
who: Superforecasters and domain experts, Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament
note: The same tournament's forecasters underestimated AI progress across the questions that have resolved so far. Its extinction estimates are on the Forecasts page.

title: Carbon dioxide removed from the air by machines in 2024
who: Superforecasters and domain experts, Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament
forecast: 0.32 to 0.60 million tonnes a year (the two groups' medians)
unit: million tonnes of CO2 a year
note: The same forecasters were too hopeful about clean-technology progress in general, while being too cautious about AI.
